summary: The issue's H200 trace identified speculative_attention_mode=prefill as the cause: Kimi-K3 DSPARK target verification used FA3, which widened FP8 KV cache chunks to BF16 on every step. The prepared base already routes supported Kimi-K3 DSPARK verification through decode on SM100/SM103, but that override exits on Hopper, so the reported H200 command still retains the faulty prefill route. This change narrowly recognizes fp8_e4m3 FlashMLA as a valid DSPARK verification backend on Hopper and resolves speculative_attention_mode to decode. Configuration-level regression and boundary tests pass; full H200 throughput validation was not possible in this environment.

tests.what_was_measured: The reported Hopper + Kimi-K3 + DSPARK + fp8_e4m3 + explicit FlashMLA decode configuration resolves target verification to decode. Independent boundaries retain prefill for FA3, BF16 FlashMLA, and non-Hopper gfx950, and the adjacent MiniMax override test remains passing. Result: 2 passed, 93 deselected.

Full model-override module: 91 passed and 4 unrelated CUDA-assumption tests failed on the prepared ROCm host (DeepSeek V4 SM100 MoE expectation, DLLM CUDA routing, MiniMax modelopt_fp4 unsupported on ROCm, and MXFP8 SM100 runner expectation). The new regression passed within this run.
Formatting/lint tool availability; the prepared interpreter does not contain the ruff module, so this check was environment-blocked before examining files. git diff --check passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned device is one AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) with ROCm 7.2. The defect and correction concern CUDA FlashMLA on H200 (SM90); running an AMD kernel would not validate that path. No model GPU execution is claimed.

remaining_limitations: No H200/SM90 GPU was available, so the 3.89x throughput regression and elimination of FP8-to-BF16 copy kernels were not independently profiled.
Kimi-K3 and Kimi-K3-DSpark weights were unavailable; no full-model semantic or performance run was performed.
Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned, so the reported TP32/EP32 four-node workload could not be reproduced.
The source issue comment supplies the corrected H200 benchmark (668.79 output tok/s versus 173.32 before), but this report treats that as upstream evidence rather than locally reproduced measurement.
No native code changed and no native rebuild was needed.
